title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text: Chapter X — Order for Maintenance of Wives, Children and Parents

title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text:
Subsection 1 > Text
If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain— (a) his wife, unable to maintain herself; or (b) his legitimate or illegitimate child, whether married or not, unable to maintain itself; or (c) his legitimate or illegitimate child (not being a married daughter) who has attained majority, where such child is, by reason of any physical or mental abnormality or injury unable to maintain itself; or (d) his father or mother, unable to maintain himself or herself, a Magistrate of the first class may, upon proof of such neglect or refusal, order such person to make a monthly allowance for the maintenance of his wife or such child, father or mother, at such monthly rate as such Magistrate thinks fit and to pay the same to such person as the Magistrate may from time to time direct.

Subsection 1 > Proviso 1
Provided that the Magistrate may order the father of a female child referred to in clause (b) to make such allowance, until she attains her majority, if the Magistrate is satisfied that the husband of such female child, if married, is not possessed of sufficient means.

Subsection 1 > Proviso 2
Provided further that the Magistrate may, during the pendency of the proceeding regarding monthly allowance for the maintenance under this sub-section, order such person to make a monthly allowance for the interim maintenance of his wife or such child, father or mother, and the expenses of such proceeding which the Magistrate considers reasonable, and to pay the same to such person as the Magistrate may from time to time direct.

title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text:
Subsection 1 > Proviso 3
Provided also that an application for the monthly allowance for the interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding under the second proviso shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of the service of notice of the application to such person.

Subsection 1 > Explanation
For the purposes of this Chapter, “wife” includes a woman who has been divorced by, or has obtained a divorce from, her husband and has not remarried.

Subsection 2
Any such allowance for the maintenance or interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding shall be payable from the date of the order, or, if so ordered, from the date of the application for maintenance or interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding, as the case may be.

Subsection 3 > Text
If any person so ordered fails without sufficient cause to comply with the order, any such Magistrate may, for every breach of the order, issue a warrant for levying the amount due in the manner provided for levying fines, and may sentence such person, for the whole or any part of each month's allowance for the maintenance or the interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding, as the case may be, remaining unpaid after the execution of the warrant, to imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or until payment if sooner made.

Subsection 3 > Proviso 1
Provided that no warrant shall be issued for the recovery of any amount due under this section unless application be made to the Court to levy such amount within a period of one year from the date on which it became due.

title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text:
Subsection 3 > Proviso 2
Provided further that if such person offers to maintain his wife on condition of her living with him, and she refuses to live with him, such Magistrate may consider any grounds of refusal stated by her, and may make an order under this section notwithstanding such offer, if he is satisfied that there is just ground for so doing.

Subsection 3 > Explanation
If a husband has contracted marriage with another woman or keeps a mistress, it shall be considered to be just ground for his wife's refusal to live with him.

Subsection 4
No wife shall be entitled to receive an allowance for the maintenance or the interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding, from her husband under this section if she is living in adultery, or if, without any sufficient reason, she refuses to live with her husband, or if they are living separately by mutual consent.

Subsection 5
On proof that any wife in whose favour an order has been made under this section is living in adultery, or that without sufficient reason she refuses to live with her husband, or that they are living separately by mutual consent, the Magistrate shall cancel the order.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
text:
Subject
Protection and processing of digital personal data

Purpose
The Act provides for processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognises an individual's right to protect personal data while allowing lawful processing.

Important Note
The Act has phased commencement under the notification dated 13 November 2025. The AI must check the applicable commencement date of a provision before representing that provision as currently operative.

Personal data in digital form.

A person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.

A person registered with the Board who enables a Data Principal to give, manage, review and withdraw consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform.

title: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
text:
Subject
Maintenance of a Hindu wife

Scope
Section 18

Chapter
Chapter III — Maintenance

Important Note
Section 18 concerns the entitlement of a Hindu wife to maintenance from her husband and circumstances in which she may live separately without forfeiting her claim.

title: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
text:
Statutory Text > Subsection 1
Subject to the provisions of this section, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Intro
A Hindu wife shall be entitled to live separately from her husband without forfeiting her claim to maintenance if:

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Grounds > Clause (a)
He is guilty of desertion, that is to say, of abandoning her without reasonable cause and without her consent or against her wish, or of wilfully neglecting her.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Grounds > Clause (b)
He has treated her with such cruelty as to cause a reasonable apprehension in her mind that it will be harmful or injurious to live with her husband.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Grounds > Clause (d)
He has any other wife living.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Grounds > Clause (e)
He keeps a concubine in the same house in which his wife is living or habitually resides with a concubine elsewhere.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Grounds > Clause (f)
He has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Grounds > Clause (g)
There is any other cause justifying her living separately.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2 > Omitted Clause
Clause (c) has been omitted.

Statutory Text > Subsection 3
A Hindu wife shall not be entitled to separate residence and maintenance from her husband if she is unchaste or ceases to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
Subject
Maintenance and alimony under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955

Scope
Sections 24 and 25

Important Note
These sections provide statutory routes within proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act. They do not establish a universal fixed percentage or mathematical formula for maintenance.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
Section 24 > Type
interim_maintenance

Section 24 > Plain Summary
Where, in a proceeding under the Hindu Marriage Act, either the wife or husband has no independent income sufficient for their support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, the court may, on application by either spouse, order the respondent to pay proceeding expenses and a reasonable monthly sum during the proceeding, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the respondent's income.

Section 24 > Statutory Text > Main Provision
Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife or the husband, order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding, and monthly during the proceeding such sum as, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the income of the respondent, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.

Section 24 > Statutory Text > Proviso
Provided that the application for the payment of the expenses of the proceeding and such monthly sum during the proceeding, shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice on the wife or the husband, as the case may be.

Section 24 > Key Elements
Applies to proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act.

Section 24 > Key Elements
Either spouse may apply.

Section 24 > Key Elements
The applicant's independent income is relevant.

Section 24 > Key Elements
The respondent's income is relevant.

Section 24 > Key Elements
The court may order payment of expenses of the proceeding.

Section 24 > Key Elements
The court may order a monthly sum during the proceeding.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25

Section 25 > Type
permanent_alimony

Section 25 > Plain Summary
A court exercising jurisdiction under the Hindu Marriage Act may, at the time of passing a decree or subsequently, on an application by either spouse, order the respondent to pay maintenance and support as a gross sum or monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant, having regard to the statutory considerations and circumstances of the case.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
Section 25 > Statutory Text > Subsection 1
Any court exercising jurisdiction under this Act may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, on application made to it for the purpose by either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, order that the respondent shall pay to the applicant for her or his maintenance and support such gross sum or such monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant as, having regard to the respondent's own income and other property, if any, the income and other property of the applicant, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just, and any such payment may be secured, if necessary, by a charge on the immovable property of the respondent.

Section 25 > Statutory Text > Subsection 2
If the court is satisfied that there is a change in the circumstances of either party at any time after it has made an order under sub-section (1), it may at the instance of either party, vary, modify or rescind any such order in such manner as the court may deem just.

Section 25 > Statutory Text > Subsection 3
If the court is satisfied that the party in whose favour an order has been made under this section has re-married or, if such party is the wife, that she has not remained chaste, or, if such party is the husband, that he has had sexual intercourse with any woman outside wedlock, it may at the instance of the other party vary, modify or rescind any such order in such manner as the court may deem just.

Section 25 > Key Elements
Either spouse may apply.

Section 25 > Key Elements
The application may be made at the time of passing a decree or subsequently.

Section 25 > Key Elements
The court may order a gross sum.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25

Subject
Maintenance rights of a divorced Muslim woman

Important Note
The Supreme Court considered whether a divorced Muslim woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and addressed the relationship between that remedy and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.

title: Mohd Abdul Samad v. State of Telangana & Anr.
text:
Issue
Whether a divorced Muslim woman can claim maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Holding
A divorced Muslim woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The Supreme Court held that the remedy under Section 125 is available to a divorced Muslim woman and is not excluded merely because she is governed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.

Important Principles
A divorced Muslim woman can invoke the maintenance remedy under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Important Principles
The remedy under Section 125 CrPC is a secular remedy and is not confined by the personal law of the parties.

Important Principles
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 does not take away the remedy available to a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 CrPC.

Important Principles
The availability of a remedy under the 1986 Act does not by itself prevent a divorced Muslim woman from seeking maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.

Important Principles
The judgment emphasizes the protective purpose of maintenance provisions and the need to prevent destitution and vagrancy.

Statutory Text > Intro
The Magistrate may, after giving the aggrieved person and the respondent an opportunity of being heard and on being prima facie satisfied that domestic violence has taken place or is likely to take place, pass a protection order in favour of the aggrieved person and prohibit the respondent from—

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (a)
Committing any act of domestic violence.

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (b)
Aiding or abetting in the commission of acts of domestic violence.

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (c)

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (d)
Attempting to communicate in any form, whatsoever, with the aggrieved person, including personal, oral or written or electronic or telephonic contact.

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (e)
Alienating any assets, operating bank lockers or bank accounts used or held or enjoyed by both parties, jointly by the aggrieved person and the respondent or singly by the respondent, including her stridhan or any other property held either jointly by the parties or separately by them, without the leave of the Magistrate.

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (f)
Causing violence to the dependants, other relatives or any person who give the aggrieved person assistance from domestic violence.

Statutory Text > Prohibitions > Clause (g)
Committing any other act as specified in the protection order.

While disposing of an application under sub-section (1) of section 12, the Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence.

Maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 or any other law for the time being in force.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2
The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.

Statutory Text > Subsection 3
The Magistrate shall have the power to order an appropriate lump sum payment or monthly payments of maintenance, as the nature and circumstances of the case may require.

Statutory Text > Subsection 4
The Magistrate shall send a copy of the order for monetary relief made under sub-section (1) to the parties to the application and to the in charge of the police station within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the respondent resides.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Section 20
text:

The respondent shall pay the monetary relief granted to the aggrieved person within the period specified in the order under sub-section (1).

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
Subject
Alimony pendente lite, permanent alimony and maintenance

Scope
Sections 36 and 37

Chapter
Chapter VII — Jurisdiction and Procedure

Important Note
Sections 36 and 37 provide statutory routes for interim and permanent financial support in proceedings under Chapter V or Chapter VI of the Special Marriage Act.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
Statutory Text > Main
Where in any proceeding under Chapter V or Chapter VI it appears to the district court that the wife has no independent income sufficient for her support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife, order the husband to pay to her the expenses of the proceeding, and weekly or monthly during the proceeding such sum as having regard to the husband's income, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.

Statutory Text > Proviso
Provided that the application for the payment of the expenses of the proceeding and such weekly or monthly sum during the proceeding under Chapter V or Chapter VI, shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice on the husband.

Plain Summary
Section 36 allows the district court, in proceedings under Chapter V or VI, to order the husband to pay the wife's proceeding expenses and a reasonable weekly or monthly amount during the proceeding when she has no independent income sufficient for her support and necessary proceeding expenses.

Key Elements
The proceeding must be under Chapter V or Chapter VI.

Key Elements
The provision applies where the wife has no independent income sufficient for her support and necessary proceeding expenses.

Key Elements
The wife may apply for relief under the section.

Key Elements
The court may order payment of expenses of the proceeding.

Key Elements
The court may order a weekly or monthly amount during the proceeding.

Key Elements
The amount is to be determined having regard to the husband's income and what appears reasonable to the court.

Key Elements
The application should, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from service of notice on the husband.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
Statutory Text > Subsection 1
Any court exercising jurisdiction under Chapter V or Chapter VI may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent to the decree, on application made to it for the purpose, order that the husband shall secure to the wife for her maintenance and support, if necessary, by a charge on the husband's property such gross sum or such monthly or periodical payment of money for a term not exceeding her life, as, having regard to her own property, if any, her husband's property and ability, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just.

Statutory Text > Subsection 2
If the district court is satisfied that there is a change in the circumstances of either party at any time after it has made an order under sub-section (1), it may, at the instance of either party, vary, modify or rescind any such order in such manner as it may seem to the court to be just.

Plain Summary
Section 37 allows a court exercising jurisdiction under Chapter V or Chapter VI to order permanent alimony and maintenance for the wife at the time of a decree or after the decree. The court considers factors including the parties' property, the husband's ability, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances.

Key Elements
The court must be exercising jurisdiction under Chapter V or Chapter VI.

Key Elements
An application may be made for permanent alimony and maintenance.

Key Elements
An order may be made when the decree is passed or after the decree.

Key Elements
The court may order a gross sum.

Key Elements
The court may order monthly or periodical payments.

Key Elements
The payment may be secured by a charge on the husband's property if necessary.
